paragraphs.ko: 먼저 선택한 이벤트의 출력부터 구별하겠습니다. 명령 목록의 화면 지우기와 그리기는 다른 역할입니다. 드로 인스턴스드를 선택하면 파란 배경 위에 색이 섞인 삼각형이 보입니다. 이제 이 결과에서 메시의 꼭짓점과 셰이더 입력으로 질문을 옮겨 보겠습니다.
paragraphs.en: First distinguish the selected event’s output. Clearing the image and drawing it have different roles in the command list. Selecting DrawInstanced reveals a colored triangle on the blue background. We now move the question from that result to mesh vertices and shader inputs.

koCues.text: 먼저 선택한 이벤트의 출력부터 구별하겠습니다.
명령 목록의 화면 지우기와 그리기는 다른 역할입니다.

드로 인스턴스드를 선택하면 파란 배경
위에 색이 섞인 삼각형이 보입니다.

이제 이 결과에서 메시의 꼭짓점과
셰이더 입력으로 질문을 옮겨 보겠습니다.

enCues.text:
First distinguish the
selected event’s output.

Clearing the image and drawing it have
different roles in the command list.

Selecting DrawInstanced reveals a
colored triangle on the blue background.

We now move the question from that result
to mesh vertices and shader inputs.

paragraphs.ko: 이번에는 우리 채널의 렌더독 시연으로 바꾸겠습니다. 선택한 삼각형과 색 입력을 먼저 확인하고, 셰이더가 같은 색을 반환하는 위치를 연결하죠. 화면의 빨간 표시는 검사할 데이터 흐름을 가리킵니다. 이 간단한 셰이더에서 확인한 연결을 다른 게임의 복잡한 조명 구현까지 확대하지는 않겠습니다.
paragraphs.en: Now switch to our channel’s RenderDoc demonstration. Identify the selected triangle and its color input, then connect them to the shader returning that same color. Our red annotation marks the data flow being inspected. A connection verified in this simple shader does not establish the implementation of a complex lighting system in another game.

koCues.text: 이번에는 우리 채널의 렌더독 시연으로 바꾸겠습니다.

선택한 삼각형과 색 입력을 먼저 확인하고,
셰이더가 같은 색을 반환하는 위치를 연결하죠.
화면의 빨간 표시는 검사할 데이터 흐름을 가리킵니다.

이 간단한 셰이더에서 확인한 연결을 다른 게임의
복잡한 조명 구현까지 확대하지는 않겠습니다.

enCues.text:
Now switch to our channel’s
RenderDoc demonstration.

Identify the selected triangle

connect them to the shader

Our red annotation marks the
data flow being inspected.

A connection verified in this
simple shader does not establish

the implementation of a complex
lighting system in another game.

paragraphs.ko: 메시와 입력을 보는 창에서는 위치와 색을 구분합니다. 위치 숫자는 삼각형의 모양과 연결되고, 색 입력은 뒤의 표현과 연결될 수 있습니다. 화면에 보이는 색 표만 보고 모든 조명값을 안다고 할 수는 없죠. 선택한 명령과 셰이더의 입력 이름이 서로 맞는지 확인하는 것이 먼저입니다.
paragraphs.en: Separate position from color in the mesh and input views. Positions relate to triangle shape, while color inputs can affect appearance. A color table does not reveal every lighting quantity. First match the selected command to its shader input names.

koCues.text: 메시와 입력을 보는 창에서는 위치와 색을 구분합니다.

위치 숫자는 삼각형의 모양과 연결되고,
색 입력은 뒤의 표현과 연결될 수 있습니다.

화면에 보이는 색 표만 보고 모든
조명값을 안다고 할 수는 없죠.

선택한 명령과 셰이더의 입력 이름이
서로 맞는지 확인하는 것이 먼저입니다.

enCues.text:
Separate position from color
in the mesh and input views.

Positions relate to triangle shape,
while color inputs can affect appearance.

A color table does not reveal
every lighting quantity.

First match the selected command
to its shader input names.

paragraphs.ko: 셰이더 단계가 바뀌면 같은 반환이라는 말도 다른 일을 가리킵니다. 꼭짓점 셰이더의 반환을 픽셀 셰이더의 최종 색으로 설명하지 않겠습니다. 지금 선택한 단계와 입력을 읽고, 다음에 남겨 둔 색 반환 시연으로 연결하세요. 자료의 이름과 만든 작업을 함께 기록해야 화면의 인상보다 구체적인 근거가 됩니다.
paragraphs.en: A return value means different things at different shader stages. Do not describe a vertex-shader return as the pixel shader’s final color. Read the selected stage and input, then connect to the retained color-return demonstration. Resource names and producing operations provide more concrete evidence than appearance alone.

koCues.text:
셰이더 단계가 바뀌면 같은 반환이라는
말도 다른 일을 가리킵니다.

꼭짓점 셰이더의 반환을 픽셀 셰이더의
최종 색으로 설명하지 않겠습니다.

지금 선택한 단계와 입력을 읽고, 다음에
남겨 둔 색 반환 시연으로 연결하세요.

자료의 이름과 만든 작업을 함께 기록해야
화면의 인상보다 구체적인 근거가 됩니다.

A return value means different
things at different shader stages.

Do not describe a vertex-shader return
as the pixel shader’s final color.

Read the selected stage
and input, then connect

to the retained
color-return demonstration.

Resource names and
producing operations provide

more concrete evidence
than appearance alone.

paragraphs.ko: 깊이 자원은 색 영상처럼 보지 말고 깊이 규칙을 확인합니다. 투영 뒤의 깊이는 일반적으로 실제 거리와 선형 관계가 아닙니다. 리버스드 지를 쓰는 경우에는 가까움과 멂의 값 관계도 달라질 수 있습니다.
paragraphs.en: Examine a depth resource using its depth convention rather than treating it as a color image. Projected depth is generally nonlinear with physical distance. Reversed-Z can also change which numerical values represent near and far surfaces.

koCues.text:
깊이 자원은 색 영상처럼 보지
말고 깊이 규칙을 확인합니다.

투영 뒤의 깊이는 일반적으로 실제
거리와 선형 관계가 아닙니다.

리버스드 지를 쓰는 경우에는 가까움과
멂의 값 관계도 달라질 수 있습니다.

enCues.text:
Examine a depth resource

Reversed-Z can also change which numerical

paragraphs.ko: 지 버퍼라면 각 채널이 무엇을 담는지 엔진의 자료와 대응합니다. 법선을 색처럼 표시해 본 화면은 시각화이지 실제 표면의 색이 아닙니다. 압축이나 인코딩 규칙을 모르면 채널의 값만으로 재질을 잘못 해석할 수 있습니다.
paragraphs.en: Match G-buffer channels to engine documentation. A normal buffer displayed as color is a visualization, not the surface's actual color. Compression and encoding must be understood before interpreting channel values as material attributes.

koCues.text:
지 버퍼라면 각 채널이 무엇을
담는지 엔진의 자료와 대응합니다.

법선을 색처럼 표시해 본 화면은
시각화이지 실제 표면의 색이 아닙니다.

압축이나 인코딩 규칙을 모르면 채널의
값만으로 재질을 잘못 해석할 수 있습니다.

enCues.text:
Match G-buffer channels
to engine documentation.

visualization, not the

paragraphs.ko: 그림자 자원에서는 어느 광원이 만들었는지와 읽는 패스를 연결합니다. 화면 픽셀에서 광원 공간으로 가는 변환과 깊이 비교가 어디에서 이루어지는지 봅니다. 캐스케이드나 페이지가 있다면 분할과 선택 기준도 따로 확인합니다.
paragraphs.en: For shadow resources, connect the producing light with the consuming pass. Locate the transformation from a screen surface to light space and its depth comparison. Cascades and pages require examination of their partitioning and selection rules.

그림자 자원에서는 어느 광원이

깊이 비교가 어디에서 이루어지는지 봅니다.

캐스케이드나 페이지가 있다면
분할과 선택 기준도 따로 확인합니다.

paragraphs.ko: 반사 패스에서는 화면 깊이를 따라간 결과와 대체 입력을 구별합니다. 화면 밖이나 가려진 곳에서 값이 없을 때 프로브나 다른 추적 결과를 읽는지 확인합니다. 반사 결과 한 장만으로 모든 표본이 같은 방식으로 계산됐다고 결론 내리지는 않습니다.
paragraphs.en: In reflection passes, distinguish screen-depth tracing from fallback inputs. Inspect whether probes or other trace results supply values for off-screen or occluded regions. A single reflection image does not prove that all samples were produced identically.

반사 패스에서는 화면 깊이를 따라간
결과와 대체 입력을 구별합니다.

화면 밖이나 가려진 곳에서 값이 없을 때
프로브나 다른 추적 결과를 읽는지 확인합니다.

반사 결과 한 장만으로 모든 표본이 같은
방식으로 계산됐다고 결론 내리지는 않습니다.

paragraphs.ko: 이번에는 언리얼 엔진의 자원 보기 창으로 바뀝니다. 여러 자료의 이름이 함께 나타나지만 모두 같은 텍스처는 아닙니다. 그림자 페이지 풀과 가상 텍스처의 물리 풀을 구분해서 읽으세요. 앞 편에서 페이지가 나뉘는 방식을 배웠다면, 이제 실제 창에서 그 자료를 어떻게 찾아보는지 연결할 수 있습니다.
paragraphs.en: Switch to Unreal’s resource viewer. Several names appear, but they do not all describe the same texture. Distinguish a shadow-page pool from a virtual-texture physical pool. The earlier page discussion now connects to locating actual resources in the viewer.

여러 자료의 이름이 함께 나타나지만
모두 같은 텍스처는 아닙니다.

그림자 페이지 풀과 가상 텍스처의
물리 풀을 구분해서 읽으세요.
앞 편에서 페이지가 나뉘는 방식을 배웠다면, 이제 실제

paragraphs.ko: 자료 이름을 찾았으면 다음에는 크기와 쓰임을 확인해야 합니다. 루멘의 방사휘도 자료와 그림자 자료를 한 덩어리의 빛이라고 뭉뚱그리지 마세요. 이름은 좋은 출발점이지만 어떤 작업이 만들고 어떤 작업이 읽는지까지 확인해야 연결이 완성됩니다. 이 창만으로 전체 프레임의 모든 의존 관계를 검증한 것은 아닙니다.
paragraphs.en: After locating a name, inspect dimensions and usage. Lumen radiance data and shadow data should not be collapsed into one generic light resource. Names start the investigation; producers and consumers complete it. This viewer alone does not verify every dependency in the frame.

koCues.text:
자료 이름을 찾았으면 다음에는
크기와 쓰임을 확인해야 합니다.

paragraphs.ko: 볼륨 자원은 화면의 색만으로 설명하기 어려울 수 있습니다. 공간 격자에 저장한 밀도와 조명, 시선 방향으로 누적한 투과율을 나누어 봅니다. 격자의 해상도와 깊이 분할이 어떤 오류와 비용에 연결되는지도 살펴봅니다.
paragraphs.en: Volume processing may require more than viewing a color image. Separate spatial density and lighting grids from view-integrated transmittance. Grid resolution and depth partitioning connect to both artifacts and cost.

paragraphs.en: Temporal processing separates history from current inputs. Inspect which resources are written for later use and how motion and depth reject samples. A single capture may omit earlier execution conditions, so its interpretive limits need documentation.

격자의 해상도와 깊이 분할이 어떤

어느 자원이 기록되고 다음 프레임에서 읽히는지,

현재 프레임만 캡처하면 보이지 않는 이전 실행

노출과 색 공간, 업스케일링 및 인터페이스
합성의 위치를 실제 패스에서 확인합니다.

모든 엔진에서 이 순서가 완전히 같다고 가정하거나
준비된 그림을 실제 캡처 결과로 표시하지는 않습니다.

이벤트를 고르면 입력 자원이 어디에서
만들어졌는지 거꾸로 추적할 수 있습니다.

출력을 만든 명령과 이후 읽는 명령을 연결하면,
자료의 역할이 기능 이름보다 구체적으로 드러납니다.

한 자원이 여러 목적에서 재사용될
수 있다는 점도 확인합니다.
다음 조절은 가상 텍스처 자료의 업로드와 관련된 것입니다.

설정 이름의 프레임이라는 단어를 보고
프레임 생성 기능이라고 혼동하면 안 됩니다.

여기서 다루는 자료가 무엇인지 먼저
구별하고, 설정과 화면 반응을 보세요.

같은 성능 관련 숫자라도 어느 작업의
예산인지에 따라 뜻이 달라집니다.

자료를 얼마나 빨리 올릴지와 한 프레임을
얼마나 빨리 그릴지는 같은 측정이 아닙니다.

캐시와 로딩 상태, 카메라 구간도
함께 기록해야 비교할 수 있죠.
실제 자원을 읽는 법까지 연결했으니, 뒤의 성능 설명에서는

한 순간의 숫자 대신 조건과 반복
측정을 기준으로 삼겠습니다.
성능은 별도로 측정합니다.

프레임 검사 도구의 캡처에는 추가 비용이나
실행 방식 변화가 있을 수 있습니다.

엔진의 지피유 프로파일러와 반복 실행으로 패스
시간과 변동 폭을 확인하고, 동일 조건에서 비교합니다.
평균만 적지 말고 실행 횟수와 변동도 적는 것이 좋습니다.

셰이더 준비와 자료 로딩이 끝났는지, 캐시가
안정됐는지, 카메라 이동 구간이 같은지도 확인합니다.

한 프레임의 숫자는 장면 전체의
성능을 대표하지 않을 수 있습니다.

검사 결과는 실제 자원과 입력과
출력의 연결로 기록해 보세요.

화면에서 관찰한 변화와 구현을
확인한 근거를 나누어 적으면,
어떤 현상을 어디까지 설명할 수 있는지 분명해집니다.

이 과정이 기술 이름을 외우는 것보다 오래
쓸 수 있는 렌더링 이해의 기준입니다.

둠의 밝기 숫자에서 출발해, 미리
저장한 빛과 실시간 그림자, 화면

기반 효과와 공간 격자, 레이와 캐시,
최종 복원까지 연결했습니다.

옛 기술이 한꺼번에 사라지고 새 기술
하나로 교체된 역사는 아니었습니다.
첫 번째 질문은 무엇을 저장하느냐였습니다.

밝기, 표면 속성, 깊이, 삼각형의 신원,
공간의 빛, 과거 프레임은 서로 다른 정보입니다.

저장한 것이 다르면 뒤 단계에서
대답할 수 있는 질문도 달라집니다.
두 번째는 어디를 검사하느냐였습니다.

화면에 남은 깊이만 보는지, 단순화한 공간 표현을
보는지, 실제 삼각형을 찾는지 구별했습니다.

화면 밖과 가려진 면, 얇은 구조에서
생기는 한계는 이 선택과 연결됩니다.
세 번째는 얼마나 계산하고 어떻게 재사용하느냐였습니다.

광원 후보와 경로 표본, 페이지와 캐시, 이전
프레임과 복원에는 각각 다른 비용과 오류가 있습니다.

계산을 언제 하느냐뿐 아니라 표현과 표본,
하드웨어와 재구성 방식도 함께 변했습니다.

다음에 게임의 빛을 볼 때에는 기술 이름만
보지 말고 이 질문들을 떠올려 보세요.

화면을 만든 자료와 계산의 연결을 이해하면, 좋아
보이는 이유와 깨지는 이유를 함께 설명할 수 있습니다.

enCues.text:
Can an attractive image tell
us how it was calculated?

We will distinguish the roles through
DLSS5, examine actual exposure

and focus demonstrations, then
inspect a frame's inputs and outputs.

Displayed frames and game
calculations have different

responsibilities; we begin with
what reconstruction is asked to do.

DLSS 4 Multi Frame Generation was
introduced in 2025 with support for adding

up to three generated frames per rendered
frame under supported conditions.
Its output is display frames; it does not

imply three additional
sets of ray samples.

In 2026, DLSS 4.5
expanded Super Resolution
and Multi Frame Generation features.

Its 6X mode must be understood as up to
five generated frames per rendered frame.

Dynamic operation considers
display targets and execution

conditions; it does not promise
6X operation on every device.

Keep one actually rendered
frame as a white block.

Adding three generated frames gives four
displayed blocks; adding five gives six.

More generated blocks do
not mean that the game

has performed its
simulation that many times.

In the recorded comparison, inspect
both the moving image and its interface.

A larger displayed
frame-rate number does not

establish more frequent
responses to input.

After this short demonstration,
separate rendered and generated

blocks again to distinguish
display updates from game updates.

DLSS 5 was announced in 2026 and became
available in NBA 2K27 in September.

NVIDIA describes using game
color, motion, and 3D guidance

to improve the appearance
of lighting and materials.

We discuss the vendor's
input-output description without

claiming our own quality
measurements of that game.

Creators can use controls
such as strength, color

treatment, and exclusions
to preserve artistic intent.

These controls connect the feature's
output to the intended design.

They should be distinguished from exact
computation of every physical light path.

Compare the same responsibility
across different games.

The first three sources are
March2026 DLSS5 previews.

Read Off and On first, then examine
the light on faces and clothing.

The September basketball
release is a separate example.

Start with Resident Evil, moving from
a dark room to the rainy vehicle shot.
Watch the turning face and wet clothing.

The labelled On condition
changes their surface appearance.

Different poses are not a
pixel-aligned ground truth.

Starfield provides an orange coat
and suits in brighter interiors.

The dialogue UI identifies a
character; it is not a quality score.

Lighting differs from the rainy
scene, but the question remains:

where does the final appearance of
light on skin and fabric change?

Hogwarts Legacy moves through an interior,
a street and an underground shot.

At each cut, select the
new face and clothing.
Compare Off and On within that shot.

A glowing wand or visible steam alone does
not establish new physical simulation.

Now examine skin, jerseys and arm
highlights on the basketball court.

The close Detroit number-two
shot changes from Off

to On; subsequent dunks
use other camera angles.

This compares displayed appearance,
not ball physics or input response.

Compare those surfaces with dark wet
clothing, a bright coat and underground

fabric: the same display-stage task
meets different surface conditions.

After comparing surfaces
in four games, establish an

observation reference in
this2022 Hogwarts showcase.

The character in yellow climbs
stairs below bright windows.

Identify the clothing,
windows and shaded wall.

Outside, the same clothing is
framed by sky and stone pillars.

The camera looks up at the
towers, then follows the stairs.

The character remains the reference, while
background and viewing direction change.

Record those conditions
when comparing images.

At the balustrade, nearby stone and
distant landscape share one image.

Red identifies the nearby rail; another
color identifies the distant view.
Looking down changes occlusion too.

This is why brightness comparisons
need the observation position as well.

The camera turns around the
character near a burning brazier.

Follow the flame, clothing
and stone floor separately.

A bright flame and a lit surface
are different observation

targets; one region alone does
not describe the entire image.

Back in the hall, the character
appears dark against a bright window.

Turning the camera moves the window and
carved decorations within the image.

Identify the window, clothing
and stairs in that order.

A consistent reference makes color
and exposure changes easier to read.

Finally, approach a
character beneath the tree.

The Talk prompt identifies
an interaction target; our

red mark identifies the
clothing under observation.

Keep the game's instructions
distinct from our comparison marks.

Throughout this progression,
actual computation, temporal

reconstruction, and display-frame
generation should remain distinct.

Comparisons record hardware support, game
version, internal resolution, and latency.

A higher version number
does not mean every

preceding function has
merged into one replacement.

We compared surface
appearance across four games.

Next, control a cause
directly: exposure and

focus can change the image
without moving lights.
Connect editor settings to results, then

inspect the actual
resources inside a frame.

Lighting results are not yet the
colors sent directly to a monitor.

Bright values can exceed
a display's range.

Exposure and tone mapping connect that
wider range to the final display range.

Separate the lighting value
from the displayed value.

An illustrative linear intensity
of two with an exposure

multiplier of one-half feeds a
value of one into tone mapping.
The light itself has not changed.

Tone mapping applies a
separate curve, so the final

display is not explained by
that multiplication alone.

Exposure scales scene brightness,
while tone mapping applies

nonlinear transformations
such as highlight compression.

Automatic exposure can change the
whole image without a lighting

change, so technical comparisons
need controlled exposure conditions.
This is a2017 Unreal editor demonstration.

Separate the cube arrangement from the
post-process controls on the right.

Camera and parameters both change, so
we first identify the edited inputs

rather than attributing every
brightness difference to one feature.
This editor demonstration adjusts exposure

settings rather than
rearranging the lights.

Follow the controls alongside
the image brightness.

It illustrates how the
displayed result can change

even when the lighting
setup remains the same.

That is why we must match exposure
before comparing reconstruction features.

The exposure panel shows lower and
upper brightness limits and a bias.

Reading those settings differs from
measuring displayed pixel intensity.

Keep the same bright and dark cube faces
in view while following the changes.

The demonstration switches
to histogram visualization.

It adds information for
reading a brightness

distribution instead of showing
only the ordinary image.
Connect the lower graph to the controls.
Its green and blue colors are

visualization, not the
wall material colors.

The visualization explicitly
names a logarithmic scale.

Equal horizontal spacing does not mean
an equal additive brightness change.

It displays a wide
dark-to-bright range in one view.

Read the scale before relating
graph position to brightness.

Camera movement changes the
proportions of surfaces in the image.
Seeing more bright cubes can change the

brightness distribution
within the same lit scene.

Exposure comparisons therefore need
camera framing as well as settings.

This is an observation demonstration,
not a fixed-camera numerical experiment.

We can now separate three
roles: edited settings,

diagnostic visualization
and the final image.

Settings are inputs; the
graph helps inspection; the

displayed image includes
later display processing.

A diagnostic graph color is not
itself a final surface pixel color.

Bloom adds the appearance of bright
regions spreading into neighboring pixels.

A glowing image does not
establish that indirect
illumination reached surrounding surfaces.

Bloom around an edge is not
proof of a light bounce.

In the bloom controls,
distinguish spread around

bright regions from the
cube surfaces themselves.
A wider glow and light bouncing onto

another surface answer
different questions.

Inspect the edited effect
rather than treating a bright

impression as proof of an
indirect-lighting implementation.
Next come color and tone controls.

The cubes remain while their
displayed appearance can be adjusted.

Earlier chapters created
scene lighting; this

stage maps its result
into a display range.

Distinguish computing the input
from shaping its presentation.

Use both a bright face and a
shaded face on the same cube.

Looking only at highlights
can miss contrast changes;

looking only at shadows can
miss highlight compression.

Follow the control and both
regions to distinguish overall

changes from changes concentrated
in a brightness range.

A darker-looking surface
does not by itself
establish that its material asset changed.

Here we observe post-process
controls and their results.

A claim about material inputs requires
inspecting those inputs separately.

Similar image changes can
originate at different stages.

Read brightness and color balance
as separate aspects of grading.

Keep the cube arrangement as a reference
and identify the chosen control.

A warmer or cooler appearance
can resemble a changed light

color without establishing
the same underlying operation.

Keeping the same surface preserves
a reference for comparison.

Red follows the observed face;
another color identifies the setting.

The mark is an observation location, not
a game-world distance or physical unit.

Reacquire the surface
when the camera changes.

Record the edited input,
the surface where a change

appears and any simultaneous
condition changes.

Next we examine a separate
color-transform resource, continuing the

distinction between final displayed
color and the original lighting value.

First locate the setting that
will apply the color transform.

The demonstrator selects the
area labelled Post Process

Blendable and searches for
blend in the right panel.

The scene cubes and the effect
settings have separate roles.

Establish where the next
resource will be connected.

The panel shows a post-process
material entry, followed by

a lookup-table asset displayed
as a strip of colors, or LUT.

It represents color correspondence rather
than a small map of the game world.

After identifying the
color resource, distinguish

distance and focus in the
same cube arrangement.

Depth of field represents
differences in focus and distance,

while motion blur approximates
movement over an exposure interval.
These effects can conceal small shadow or

reflection errors or
introduce their own blur.

Comparisons should distinguish
enabled and disabled conditions.

Before reading focus regions, inspect
what becomes blurred in the ordinary view.

Use the cube arrangement to
distinguish near and far edges.

The Scale control changes
the amount of blur.

This is a historical2017
Bokeh demonstration;
its value is not a physical camera f-stop.

Visible blur alone does not identify
the responsible distance region.

The visualization menu therefore
leads to a focus-region display.
Once diagnostic colors and their legend

appear, distinguish them
from material colors.

We can then inspect the focus
reference and the boundaries around it.

Read the focus legend first:
blue marks far regions,

green near regions and
black the focused region.
These are not cube material colors.

As distance and transition
settings are edited, distinguish

the focus reference from
the width of its transition.

Focus distance and transition
width are not the same quantity.
One establishes a reference location; the

other relates to the
surrounding change range.

Read the edited field before inspecting
the affected regions, without

pairing different settings as an
identical-condition On/Off comparison.
Next, inspect focus.

Separate near, focused and far
regions in the debug view, then

return to the scene and observe
blur on the nearer object.

Here the blur is connected
to focus controls.

Recording those conditions
prevents us from confusing

it with a reconstruction
error in a reflection.

Back in the ordinary view, a
nearer cube appears blurred.

Separate diagnostic colors
from ordinary scene colors.

Camera and focus-related
settings also change in this

demonstration, so record those
conditions when explaining the blur.

When focus effects are
enabled during reconstruction

comparisons, a blurred
edge can be misattributed.

Check focus and camera conditions first,
then the reconstruction conditions.

Separating stages lets similar-looking
blur be explained by different causes.

The later editor interval retains
the cube arrangement as a reference.

Follow the selected control and
compare near and far surfaces.

An overall impression of blur can
hide which distance region changed.

Separating the focus
reference and its surrounding

regions makes the
observation more specific.

Read the input name, locate its change,
then inspect the affected surface.
Record camera changes separately.

This observation method transfers
to other engines without

assuming their internal
post-process order is identical.

Check again whether color inputs
represent linear values or display values.

This closes the linear-space
discussion from episode two.

Missing or duplicated
transformations at texture input,

lighting, and final output
produce incorrect brightness.

Final pixels combine geometry,
visibility, lighting,

materials, reconstruction,
and post-processing.

We can now examine how to trace those
connections during frame inspection.
We compared final appearance in four games

with editor exposure,
color and focus controls.

We can observe changes,
but identifying which

command read which resource
is another question.

Frame inspection now
follows actual inputs and

outputs rather than
relying on feature names.

Before frame inspection, briefly follow
the code that submits drawing commands.

Distinguish the debugger’s
yellow current-line
mark from the caller list below it.

The source connects closing a command
list with requesting execution.

A CPU paused on this line does
not establish GPU completion.

Feature names alone do not determine
a frame's actual structure.

Engine version, platform, rendering
path, and settings can change its passes.

A frame debugger such as
RenderDoc helps inspect

commands and resources
from a captured frame.

This is our channel’s simple
DirectX12 demonstration,

not evidence of a complex
game lighting implementation.

Separate the frame inspection
window from its event list and

follow how selecting an
operation exposes different data.

We connect a visible shape with
the command that produced it.

Start with a comparison question:
whether reflections retain off-screen

objects, how shadow pages are updated,
or which attributes a G-buffer stores.

A specific question determines
what to inspect among many events.
Event names guide inspection.

Clearing an image and drawing a
triangle have different roles.

Start with the result being investigated,
then select its producing operation.

An item appearing in a list does not
establish that it affected every pixel.

Record execution conditions: engine
version, graphics API, rendering

path, internal and output resolution,
camera, and feature settings.

Frames captured under differing conditions
cannot easily isolate a single cause.
When opening a resource, inspect

dimensions, format,
layers, and mip levels.

Determine whether it is
screen-sized, light-space
data, or a paged or layered structure.

Names provide clues, but contents and
usage relationships need verification.

First distinguish the
selected event’s output.

Clearing the image and drawing it have
different roles in the command list.

Selecting DrawInstanced reveals a
colored triangle on the blue background.

We now move the question from that result
to mesh vertices and shader inputs.

In the recorded RenderDoc demonstration,
follow the selected triangle

draw and then the pixel shader’s
color input and return value.

This shader simply
returns its input color.

Locate the matching numbers as
they move from input to output.

This example teaches
inspection, rather than
demonstrating an entire lighting pipeline.

Separate position from color
in the mesh and input views.

Positions relate to triangle shape,
while color inputs can affect appearance.

A color table does not reveal
every lighting quantity.

First match the selected command
to its shader input names.

A return value means different
things at different shader stages.

Do not describe a vertex-shader return
as the pixel shader’s final color.

Read the selected stage
and input, then connect

to the retained
color-return demonstration.

Resource names and
producing operations provide

more concrete evidence
than appearance alone.

Now switch to our channel’s
RenderDoc demonstration.

Identify the selected triangle
and its color input, then

connect them to the shader
returning that same color.

Our red annotation marks the
data flow being inspected.

A connection verified in this
simple shader does not establish

the implementation of a complex
lighting system in another game.

Examine a depth resource
using its depth convention
rather than treating it as a color image.

Projected depth is generally
nonlinear with physical distance.

Reversed-Z can also change which numerical
values represent near and far surfaces.

Match G-buffer channels
to engine documentation.
A normal buffer displayed as color is a

visualization, not the
surface's actual color.

Compression and encoding
must be understood before

interpreting channel values
as material attributes.

For shadow resources, connect the
producing light with the consuming pass.

Locate the transformation
from a screen surface
to light space and its depth comparison.

Cascades and pages require examination of
their partitioning and selection rules.
Switch to Unreal’s resource viewer.

Several names appear, but they do
not all describe the same texture.

Distinguish a shadow-page pool from
a virtual-texture physical pool.
The earlier page discussion now connects

to locating actual
resources in the viewer.

After locating a name,
inspect dimensions and usage.

Lumen radiance data and
shadow data should not

be collapsed into one
generic light resource.

Names start the investigation;
producers and consumers complete it.

This viewer alone does not verify
every dependency in the frame.

In reflection passes, distinguish
screen-depth tracing from fallback inputs.

Inspect whether probes
or other trace results

supply values for off-screen
or occluded regions.
A single reflection image does not prove

that all samples were
produced identically.

Volume processing may require
more than viewing a color image.

Separate spatial density and lighting
grids from view-integrated transmittance.

Grid resolution and depth partitioning
connect to both artifacts and cost.

Temporal processing separates
history from current inputs.

Inspect which resources
are written for later

use and how motion and
depth reject samples.

A single capture may omit
earlier execution conditions,

so its interpretive
limits need documentation.

Compare color before
and after tone mapping.

Locate exposure, color-space
conversion, upscaling,

and interface compositing
in the actual passes.

Do not assume an identical
order in every engine

or label a prepared diagram
as a captured result.

Selecting an event allows
its input resources
to be traced back to their producers.

Connecting producing and
consuming commands reveals a

resource's role more
concretely than a feature name.

Resources can also be reused
for multiple purposes.

The next control concerns
virtual-texture uploads.

The word frame in its name does
not make it frame generation.
Identify the data being handled before

relating the setting to
the visible response.

Performance-related numbers
mean different things

depending on which task
receives the budget.

How quickly resources
upload and how quickly

a frame renders are
different measurements.

Record cache, loading
and camera conditions.

Having connected the resource
view to its controls, the

retained performance discussion
now uses conditions and

repeated measurements rather
than one instantaneous number.
Performance requires separate measurement.

Frame capture can introduce overhead
or change execution behavior.

Use the engine's GPU profiler
and repeated runs to inspect

pass timing and variability
under matched conditions.

Report sample count and
variation alongside averages.

Check shader preparation, loading,
cache state, and matched camera paths.

A single frame's timing may
not represent an entire scene.

Record the connections among actual
resources, inputs, and outputs.

Separating visual observations
from implementation

evidence makes the scope
of each conclusion clear.
This method provides a more reusable

understanding than
memorizing feature names.

We connected DOOM's brightness values
to baked lighting, real-time shadows,

screen-space effects, spatial grids,
rays, caches, and final reconstruction.

This was not a history in
which every older technique

disappeared simultaneously
into one replacement.
Our first question was what gets stored.

Brightness, surface attributes,
depth, triangle identity, spatial

lighting, and frame history
contain different information.

Different storage determines which
questions later stages can answer.

Our second question was where
the renderer searches: screen

depth, a simplified spatial
representation, or actual triangles.

Limitations involving
off-screen objects, hidden

surfaces, and thin structures
follow from this choice.

Our third question was how much gets
computed and how results are reused.

Light candidates, path samples,
pages, caches, history,

and reconstruction have
different costs and errors.

Timing changed alongside representation,
sampling, hardware, and reconstruction.

When you next examine game lighting,
think beyond a feature name.

Understanding the data and
calculations behind an image

helps explain both why it looks
convincing and why it breaks.
